{"id":"SMA-585","uuid":"e87dea71-f32a-4ffd-aafb-27e38eec8e87","title":"responses_tool_call.txt carries a trailing `data: [DONE]` its provenance header does not account for","description":"Surfaced by <issue id="1f92f811-7611-4138-aa57-b21d4dc5cc83" label="SMA-562" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-562/openairesponses-reports-finishtoolcalls-for-a-function-call-that" /> while transcribing a new CAPTURED fixture into the same directory. Not a test failure — a provenance-accuracy gap in an artifact whose whole value is being trustworthy.

## The discrepancy

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt` ends with:

```
data: [DONE]
```

Its provenance header states it is `CAPTURED against a real https://api.openai.com/v1/responses request, model gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 … on 2026-08-20`, and is explicit that

> a fixture claiming to be CAPTURED should stay faithful to what the wire actually sent, not just to what the parser happens to need.

It then enumerates **"Three kinds of trimming from the raw capture, all deliberate"** — dropped `response.created`/`response.in_progress`, dropped `obfuscation` fields, and a reduced `response` object (listing all 27 omitted keys by name). It is meticulous about removals and says nothing about the trailing `[DONE]`, because the header's structure has a slot for *trims* and none for *additions*.

## The evidence it may not have been sent

Four raw captures were taken on 2026-08-22 with `curl` against the same endpoint (`gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-5-mini`, a `background: true` request, and a resumed stream). **None of the four contains** `[DONE]` — each ends on `response.completed` followed by a blank line.

That was verified rather than assumed: the byte-faithful capture was served through this directory's wiremock harness both as-is and with `data: [DONE]\n\n` appended, and the stream terminates **identically and cleanly either way** — async-openai ends the stream on body end, so the sentinel is not required by the parser. The new fixture `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt` (added in <issue id="1f92f811-7611-4138-aa57-b21d4dc5cc83" label="SMA-562" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-562/openairesponses-reports-finishtoolcalls-for-a-function-call-that" />) is therefore shipped byte-faithful with no sentinel, and its header flags this discrepancy as a follow-up.

Note the Chat Completions API *does* send `data: [DONE]` — the four `chat_*.txt` fixtures in the same directory are presumably correct. This is specifically about the Responses API.

## Two possible causes, and they need different fixes

1. **OpenAI sent it on 2026-08-20 and stopped by 2026-08-22.** Then the fixture is faithful to its capture date and only needs a header note pinning the observed behaviour to that date. This would also be worth knowing on its own.
2. **It was appended to match the sibling** `chat_*.txt` **fixtures**, and the trim-only header structure had nowhere to disclose an addition. Then the fixture is not byte-faithful and the `CAPTURED` label overstates it.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

Nothing breaks today. But this directory's fixtures are load-bearing: <issue id="9280dbb2-ab9c-4772-b566-0736392203ae" label="SMA-522" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-522/openai-provider-emits-finish-before-usage-violating-the-core-event" />'s Gemini `FragmentedToolName` fixture went wrong precisely by being derived rather than captured, and this fixture's own header cites that incident as its reason for existing. A `CAPTURED` label that is even slightly overstated erodes the thing the label is for.

## Suggested resolution

* Re-capture a `get_weather`-style tool call against `/v1/responses` and settle empirically whether `[DONE]` is sent.
* Depending on the answer, either add a dated note to the header, or drop the line and record the removal.
* **Extend the provenance-header convention to cover additions as well as trims** — the current three-kinds-of-trimming structure cannot express "and one line was added", which is how this went unrecorded in the first place.
* While there: the same audit applies to the other `responses_*.txt` fixtures (`responses_reasoning_then_text.txt`, `responses_incomplete_length.txt`, `responses_incomplete_filter.txt`, `responses_failed.txt`), which all end in `[DONE]` too.

No production code is implicated — `ResponsesTranslator` handles both shapes correctly, which <issue id="1f92f811-7611-4138-aa57-b21d4dc5cc83" label="SMA-562" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-562/openairesponses-reports-finishtoolcalls-for-a-function-call-that" /> verified.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-585/responses-tool-calltxt-carries-a-trailing-data-done-its-provenance","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-585-responses_tool_calltxt-carries-a-trailing","createdAt":"2026-08-23T08:44:36.009Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-20T14:22:47.429Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":null,"canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"Backlog","statusType":"backlog","labels":["area:providers","stage:3","Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"stateHistory":[{"state":{"id":"46bb932e-d4b2-4e1a-8a2a-48ca21321735","name":"Backlog","type":"backlog"},"startedAt":"2026-08-23T08:44:36.009Z","endedAt":null}],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e","relations":{"blocks":[],"blockedBy":[],"relatedTo":[{"id":"SMA-562","title":"openai/responses reports Finish{ToolCalls} for a function call that streams no argument deltas"},{"id":"SMA-522","title":"OpenAI provider emits Finish before Usage, violating the core event-ordering contract"}],"duplicateOf":null}}

{"id":"SMA-585","uuid":"e87dea71-f32a-4ffd-aafb-27e38eec8e87","title":"responses_tool_call.txt carries a trailing `data: [DONE]` its provenance header does not account for","description":"Surfaced by <issue id="1f92f811-7611-4138-aa57-b21d4dc5cc83" label="SMA-562" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-562/openairesponses-reports-finishtoolcalls-for-a-function-call-that" /> while transcribing a new CAPTURED fixture into the same directory. Not a test failure — a provenance-accuracy gap in an artifact whose whole value is being trustworthy.

## The discrepancy

`crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt` ends with:

```
data: [DONE]
```

Its provenance header states it is `CAPTURED against a real https://api.openai.com/v1/responses request, model gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 … on 2026-08-20`, and is explicit that

> a fixture claiming to be CAPTURED should stay faithful to what the wire actually sent, not just to what the parser happens to need.

It then enumerates **"Three kinds of trimming from the raw capture, all deliberate"** — dropped `response.created`/`response.in_progress`, dropped `obfuscation` fields, and a reduced `response` object (listing all 27 omitted keys by name). It is meticulous about removals and says nothing about the trailing `[DONE]`, because the header's structure has a slot for *trims* and none for *additions*.

## The evidence it may not have been sent

Four raw captures were taken on 2026-08-22 with `curl` against the same endpoint (`gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-5-mini`, a `background: true` request, and a resumed stream). **None of the four contains** `[DONE]` — each ends on `response.completed` followed by a blank line.

That was verified rather than assumed: the byte-faithful capture was served through this directory's wiremock harness both as-is and with `data: [DONE]\n\n` appended, and the stream terminates **identically and cleanly either way** — async-openai ends the stream on body end, so the sentinel is not required by the parser. The new fixture `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt` (added in <issue id="1f92f811-7611-4138-aa57-b21d4dc5cc83" label="SMA-562" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-562/openairesponses-reports-finishtoolcalls-for-a-function-call-that" />) is therefore shipped byte-faithful with no sentinel, and its header flags this discrepancy as a follow-up.

Note the Chat Completions API *does* send `data: [DONE]` — the four `chat_*.txt` fixtures in the same directory are presumably correct. This is specifically about the Responses API.

## Two possible causes, and they need different fixes

1. **OpenAI sent it on 2026-08-20 and stopped by 2026-08-22.** Then the fixture is faithful to its capture date and only needs a header note pinning the observed behaviour to that date. This would also be worth knowing on its own.
2. **It was appended to match the sibling** `chat_*.txt` **fixtures**, and the trim-only header structure had nowhere to disclose an addition. Then the fixture is not byte-faithful and the `CAPTURED` label overstates it.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

Nothing breaks today. But this directory's fixtures are load-bearing: <issue id="9280dbb2-ab9c-4772-b566-0736392203ae" label="SMA-522" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-522/openai-provider-emits-finish-before-usage-violating-the-core-event" />'s Gemini `FragmentedToolName` fixture went wrong precisely by being derived rather than captured, and this fixture's own header cites that incident as its reason for existing. A `CAPTURED` label that is even slightly overstated erodes the thing the label is for.

## Suggested resolution

* Re-capture a `get_weather`-style tool call against `/v1/responses` and settle empirically whether `[DONE]` is sent.
* Depending on the answer, either add a dated note to the header, or drop the line and record the removal.
* **Extend the provenance-header convention to cover additions as well as trims** — the current three-kinds-of-trimming structure cannot express "and one line was added", which is how this went unrecorded in the first place.
* While there: the same audit applies to the other `responses_*.txt` fixtures (`responses_reasoning_then_text.txt`, `responses_incomplete_length.txt`, `responses_incomplete_filter.txt`, `responses_failed.txt`), which all end in `[DONE]` too.

No production code is implicated — `ResponsesTranslator` handles both shapes correctly, which <issue id="1f92f811-7611-4138-aa57-b21d4dc5cc83" label="SMA-562" href="https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-562/openairesponses-reports-finishtoolcalls-for-a-function-call-that" /> verified.","priority":{"value":4,"name":"Low"},"url":"https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-585/responses-tool-calltxt-carries-a-trailing-data-done-its-provenance","gitBranchName":"feature/sma-585-responses_tool_calltxt-carries-a-trailing","createdAt":"2026-08-23T08:44:36.009Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-21T16:49:16.284Z","archivedAt":null,"completedAt":null,"startedAt":"2026-11-21T16:49:16.275Z","canceledAt":null,"dueDate":null,"slaStartedAt":null,"slaMediumRiskAt":null,"slaHighRiskAt":null,"slaBreachesAt":null,"status":"In Progress","statusType":"started","labels":["area:providers","stage:3","Improvement"],"attachments":[],"documents":[],"createdBy":"Sven Maschek","createdById":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","assignee":"Sven Maschek","assigneeId":"ba6021cb-56c5-43aa-9797-fab3599d7ead","project":"Paigasus Helikon","projectId":"5d1fd72d-af2d-40f5-b562-fa04f8018610","team":"Sven Maschek","teamId":"7178572e-d61f-4cf0-bbcb-4e03c8d9f39e"}

11:: frames, leaving `Finish{ToolCalls}` with no `ToolCallDelta` to match it. It

15:: deltas -- which has no `output_item.added` either, so it cannot be served
16:: from this directory's POST-only wiremock harness and is driven as typed
17:: events in `backend/responses.rs`'s test module instead.

20:: the translator already had, so that if OpenAI ever elides the `{}` delta the

27:: longer true. For this real captured stream shape -- which does carry a

29:: `response.completed` sweep, that synthesises a ToolCallDelta from the
30:: terminal item for any call that streamed no argument deltas at all (the
31:: sweep is a dedup no-op here; it only synthesises when a stream lacks an
32:: `output_item.done`), so a live stream WITH the `{}` delta

34:: through the public API -- the two wire shapes are indistinguishable
35:: downstream of the translator. That is the fix working as intended, not a
36:: gap, but it does mean the elision this fixture guards against is no longer
37:: observable through the public ModelEvent stream, by either the live test or
38:: this fixture. The live test's real value is now an end-to-end pin against
39:: the live API (name, args, finish reason), not a change-detector for the
40:: `{}` delta specifically.

1:: Provenance: CAPTURED against a real https://api.openai.com/v1/responses
2:: request, model gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, a single `get_weather` tool, on
3:: 2026-08-20. This is the shape SMA-533's Task 12 was originally BLOCKED
4:: without: the stream conformance suite
5:: (tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs, `openai_responses`
6:: module, `ToolCallCleanStop` scenario) needs a tool-call shape, and no
7:: capture existed anywhere in the repo -- deriving one from this crate's own
8:: unit tests instead of escalating is exactly how the FragmentedToolName
9:: Gemini fixture went wrong under SMA-522 (see that module's doc comment).
10:: This capture supersedes that risk for the Responses backend.
11::
12:: Confirms `item_to_call` (backend/responses.rs) is correctly keyed on
13:: `item.id` (`fc_...`), not `call_id` (`call_...`): `output_item.added`
14:: carries both, separately, and `function_call_arguments.delta` carries only
15:: `item_id`. Also confirms arguments stream as multiple small fragments
16:: (`{"`, `city`, `":"`, `Berlin`, `"}`) rather than arriving whole, and that
17:: `response.completed` reports `"status":"completed"` with
18:: `"incomplete_details":null` for a turn whose only output is a function
19:: call -- the shape that exposed `terminal_events` reporting `Finish{Stop}`
20:: instead of `Finish{ToolCalls}` for a tool-only turn (fixed in the same
21:: SMA-533 PR that adds this fixture; see `ResponsesTranslator`'s tests
22:: module, and `tool_call_turn_finishes_with_tool_calls` in
23:: `responses_streaming.rs`, which exercises this exact fixture end to end).
24::
25:: `event:` lines are kept, unlike this directory's other `responses_*.txt`
26:: fixtures. Those omit them; async-openai's `ResponseStreamEvent` is
27:: `#[serde(tag = "type")]`, so the parser dispatches purely off the JSON
28:: `type` key inside `data:` and the `event:` line is cosmetic to it -- but
29:: this fixture is a literal transcription of a real capture that DID send
30:: them, and (per this crate's `anthropic`-sibling module's own reasoning
31:: for the same choice in the stream conformance suite) a fixture claiming
32:: to be CAPTURED should stay faithful to what the wire actually sent, not
33:: just to what the parser happens to need.
34::
35:: Three kinds of trimming from the raw capture, all deliberate:
36::
37:: 1. `response.created` and `response.in_progress` are dropped.
38::    `ResponsesTranslator::consume` has no arm for either (both fall through
39::    to the trailing `other` debug-log arm), and every fixture already
40::    committed in this directory starts at the first translator-relevant
41::    event for the same reason (compare `responses_reasoning_then_text.txt`).
42::
43:: 2. Every delta in the raw capture also carried an `"obfuscation"` field --
44::    an opaque per-chunk padding string OpenAI adds to streaming responses
45::    (documented at platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses-streaming
46::    as anti-side-channel padding, not response data). It has no
47::    corresponding field on `ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDeltaEvent` to
48::    deserialize into -- deserialization tolerates it silently either way,
49::    since none of these event structs are `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`
50::    -- but it carries no semantic content and is not stable API surface,
51::    so it is dropped here for the same reason this directory's other
52::    fixtures already omit every optional field the translator does not
53::    read (no `logprobs`, no `metadata`, a minimal `output`).
54::
55:: 3. `response.completed`'s `.response` object is reduced from the 35 keys
56::    the raw capture sends to the 8 this fixture keeps (`created_at`, `id`,
57::    `incomplete_details`, `model`, `object`, `output`, `status`, `usage`)
58::    -- the same "only what the translator reads" convention as (1) and (2)
59::    above, and as `responses_reasoning_then_text.txt`. This is NOT a "two
60::    omissions" story: the other 27 keys are absent from this fixture but
61::    present on the real wire, and their absence here should not be read
62::    as absence there. For the record, they are: `background`,
63::    `completed_at`, `error`, `frequency_penalty`, `instructions`,
64::    `max_output_tokens`, `max_tool_calls`, `metadata`, `moderation`,
65::    `parallel_tool_calls`, `presence_penalty`, `previous_response_id`,
66::    `prompt_cache_key`, `prompt_cache_retention`, `reasoning`,
67::    `safety_identifier`, `service_tier`, `store`, `temperature`, `text`,
68::    `tool_choice`, `tool_usage`, `tools`, `top_logprobs`, `top_p`,
69::    `truncation`, and `user`. The same trimming happens one level deeper:
70::    the raw capture's `usage.input_tokens_details` carries both
71::    `cached_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`; this fixture keeps only
72::    `cached_tokens`. OpenAI does send `cache_write_tokens` on the wire --
73::    it just is not consumed by the translator, so it is not reproduced
74::    here. Don't read its absence from this file as evidence OpenAI omits
75::    it.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/smaschek/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/7.0.2/skills/brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

Before you start implementing, you must, in order:

1. Lay out the approaches in a message of their own, and have your
   human partner pick one (see Lay out the approaches).
2. Write the design doc, short or full (see Size the Work).
3. Get their approval of that doc.
4. Invoke the superpowers:writing-plans skill.

If nothing is open when you write your first message and there's one
sensible way, steps 1 to 3 happen in that message (see Your First
Message).

Two things aren't implementing: a spike they said yes to (see Spike to
feel things out), and doing what they asked once they've opted out of
the questions.

## Look Before You Ask

In an existing project, or when they've given you context (a spec, a plan,
a handoff, files they pointed at, earlier conversation), dig in before your
first message. Read what they referred to and the code or material it
connects to, and keep reading until you can explain how the relevant
parts work today and what this change would touch. Never ask what the
project or their context already answers, or reopen what they've
already decided.

## Your First Message

Move the work forward, with one of these:

- **They've already said what they want** (a spec, a plan, a detailed
  request): aim for about 200 words for the whole message. Echo their
  request back in your own words, so they can see whether you've got its
  shape: what they want, who it's for, and why, as far as they've said.
  Add what you found that bears on it: how the relevant parts work today
  and what the change would touch. If you found something they may not
  have considered that would change what they're asking for or how it
  has to be built, like a constraint, a conflict, or a cheaper path, say
  so plainly. How to build it comes later, once you understand what they
  want (see Lay out the approaches). End with one line inviting
  corrections. Then, if they haven't told you why they want it, even if
  you can guess, ask about that: one open question in their own terms,
  with nothing to pick from. If they have told you, and their request
  and the project leave open something whose answer would change what
  gets built, ask about the one that would change it most; when its
  choices can be named, sketch each concretely, with what it trades off
  and which you'd pick. If nothing like that is open, there's one
  sensible way: end with the short design itself (the approach, a line on
  why the others don't fit, and the design in a few lines) and ask them
  to approve it. Their approval covers the approach and the design: write

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SMA-585: capture raw /v1/responses SSE streams, byte-faithful, to settle
# whether the endpoint sends a trailing `data: [DONE]`.
# Needs OPENAI_API_KEY in the environment. Never prints the key.
set -euo pipefail
: "${OPENAI_API_KEY:?OPENAI_API_KEY is not set}"
OUT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/out"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
STAMP="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
echo "capture time (UTC): $STAMP" > "$OUT/STAMP.txt"

cap() { # name, json body
  local name="$1" body="$2"
  curl -sS -N --max-time 120 https://api.openai.com/v1/responses \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -D "$OUT/$name.headers" \
    -d "$body" -o "$OUT/$name.sse"
  printf '%-28s bytes=%-6s status=%s  DONE-lines=%s  last-event=%s\n' \
    "$name" "$(wc -c <"$OUT/$name.sse" | tr -d ' ')" \
    "$(head -1 "$OUT/$name.headers" | tr -d '\r')" \
    "$(grep -c '^data: \[DONE\]' "$OUT/$name.sse" || true)" \
    "$(grep '^event: ' "$OUT/$name.sse" | tail -1 | cut -c8-)"
}

# 1. Same shape as responses_tool_call.txt (2026-08-20): one get_weather tool.
cap tool_call_gpt-4o-mini '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","stream":true,
 "input":"What is the weather in Berlin?",
 "tools":[{"type":"function","name":"get_weather","description":"Get the current weather for a city.",
  "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}},"required":["city"],"additionalProperties":false},"strict":true}]}'

I have the facts now. Here are the approaches.

**The facts that decide it**

- Captures from 2026-08-22 and 2026-11-21 contain no `[DONE]`. We cannot know what the endpoint sent on 2026-08-20, because no raw copy exists. Cause 1 ("OpenAI sent it then stopped") is therefore not proven, and two later captures speak against it.
- The convention is not written down in one place. Each fixture header carries it. `CONTRIBUTING.md` is the single source of truth for contributor policies.

**Approach A — correct the existing files (my recommendation)**

1. `responses_tool_call.txt`: keep the 2026-08-20 transcription. Remove `data: [DONE]`. Change the header's "Three kinds of trimming" into two fixed lists, "Removed" and "Added", with "Added: nothing" written explicitly. Add a dated note: the line was removed on 2026-11-21, with the evidence.
2. The four hand-authored fixtures: remove `[DONE]` and add a short header that says "HAND-AUTHORED (SMA-316), not captured". It also says that the terminator follows the real captures.
3. Conformance suite: remove `done()` and its two uses in `openai_responses`, and correct the doc comments. Update the line citations (78, 81–93, 96, 99), because the new header moves those lines.
4. `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt`: change the "leaves … unexplained" paragraph to point to the resolution.
5. Add a short "Wire-format fixtures" section to `CONTRIBUTING.md`: every edit is listed as Removed or Added, and a header must state "Added: nothing" when nothing was added.

Trade-off: the fixtures keep their current ids and values, so no test assertion changes.

**Approach B — replace with the new captures.** This gives byte-faithful files for tool call, reasoning and length. But the tests and the conformance suite assert on the current ids, models and token counts, so many assertions must change. `failed` and `content_filter` cannot be triggered on demand, so two fixtures stay hand-authored anyway. The diff is large for a Low-priority ticket.

**Approach C — only add notes, keep `[DONE]`.** This is the smallest change. But a fixture that says "CAPTURED" would still carry a line that the wire does not send. That is the problem the ticket exists to remove.

Chat fixtures stay unchanged, because Chat Completions does send `[DONE]`. I do not commit the raw captures. This is a small change, so the design document will be short.

Which approach do you want? I recommend A.

# SMA-585: The Responses API sends no `data: [DONE]` (design)

## Intent

The OpenAI Responses fixtures must not claim more than the wire sent.
`responses_tool_call.txt` is labelled CAPTURED and lists every trim from the
raw capture, but it ends with `data: [DONE]` and its header does not explain
that line. The header structure has a place for removals and no place for
additions, so the line went unrecorded.

These fixtures are load-bearing. SMA-522 went wrong because a fixture was
derived and not captured. A CAPTURED label that overstates its file erodes
the reason the label exists.

## Evidence

- **2026-08-22** (from SMA-562): four `curl` captures against
  `/v1/responses` (`gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-5-mini`, a `background: true`
  request, a resumed stream). None contains `[DONE]`.
- **2026-11-21** (this ticket, 16:58 UTC, `openai-version: 2020-10-01`):
  four more captures. Each ends on its terminal event followed by `\n\n`.
  None contains the string `DONE` anywhere.

  | Request | Model | Terminal event |
  |---|---|---|
  | one `get_weather` tool (same shape as the 2026-08-20 fixture) | `gpt-4o-mini` | `response.completed` |
  | plain text | `gpt-4o-mini` | `response.completed` |
  | reasoning with `summary: auto` | `gpt-5-mini` | `response.completed` |
  | `max_output_tokens: 16` | `gpt-4o-mini` | `response.incomplete` |

- No raw copy of the 2026-08-20 capture exists in the repo or in any spec or
  plan. What the endpoint sent on that date cannot be proven. Two later
  captures on two dates speak against "OpenAI sent it then stopped".
- The other four `responses_*.txt` fixtures have no provenance header. The
  SMA-316 spec (`2026-05-26-sma-316-openai-provider-design.md`, line 365)
  says they are "Hand-authored". Their `[DONE]` is an assumption copied from
  the Chat Completions shape.
- The parser does not need the sentinel. SMA-562 served the byte-faithful
  capture through the wiremock harness with and without `[DONE]`, and the
  stream ended identically. async-openai ends the stream on body end.

The raw 2026-11-21 captures are not committed. They are evidence for this
decision, and the table above records what they show.

## Goals

1. No Responses fixture or Responses test body sends `data: [DONE]`.
2. Every Responses fixture header states its provenance: CAPTURED or
   HAND-AUTHORED.
3. The header convention records additions as well as removals, and the rule
   is written down once in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
4. Every cross-reference to a fixture (line numbers, doc comments) stays
   true after the edit.

## Non-goals

- Chat Completions fixtures and tests (`chat_*.txt`, `cancellation.rs`,
  `chat_wire.rs`). Chat Completions does send `[DONE]`.
- Replacing the fixtures with the new captures (approach B, rejected below).
- Fixture headers in other provider crates. The `CONTRIBUTING.md` rule
  applies to them from now on; this ticket does not audit them.
- Production code. `ResponsesTranslator` handles both shapes.

## Anti-goals

- A test that passes only because of `[DONE]`. If a test changes behaviour
  when the sentinel goes, stop and investigate. Do not add the line back.
- Changing any asserted id, model or token count.

## Approaches

- **A. Correct the existing files (chosen).** Keep the 2026-08-20
  transcription and the current hand-authored values. Remove the sentinel,
  restructure the headers, and update the cross-references. No test
  assertion changes.
- **B. Replace with the new captures (rejected).** This gives byte-faithful
  files for three shapes. But the tests and the conformance suite assert on
  the current ids, models and token counts, so many assertions must change.
  `response.failed` and a content-filter refusal cannot be triggered on
  demand, so two fixtures stay hand-authored anyway. The diff is too large
  for a Low-priority ticket.
- **C. Add notes and keep `[DONE]` (rejected).** A CAPTURED file would still
  carry a line that the wire does not send. That is the defect this ticket
  removes.

Sven picked A on 2026-11-21.

## Design

All paths are relative to `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/` unless
stated otherwise.

1. **`tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt`.** Remove the trailing
   `data: [DONE]` line. Replace "Three kinds of trimming from the raw
   capture" with an "Edits from the raw capture" section that has two fixed
   parts:
   - **Removed:** the three existing trims, with their text kept.
   - **Added:** "nothing".
   Add a dated correction note: until 2026-11-21 this file ended with
   `data: [DONE]`, which no header entry accounted for. The note gives the
   evidence above in short form and says the line was removed on 2026-11-21.
2. **The four hand-authored fixtures** (`responses_reasoning_then_text.txt`,
   `responses_incomplete_length.txt`, `responses_incomplete_filter.txt`,
   `responses_failed.txt`). Remove the trailing `data: [DONE]`. Add a short
   `:` comment header: HAND-AUTHORED under SMA-316, not captured; the event
   shapes follow the async-openai types; the stream ends on the terminal
   event with no `[DONE]`, as the 2026-08-22 and 2026-11-21 captures show.
3. **Responses test bodies.**
   - a. `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs`, module
     `openai_responses`: remove `done()` and its two uses (`CleanStop`,
     `ToolCallCleanStop`). Correct the doc comments that cite `[DONE]` as
     "the stream terminator every committed fixture in this crate ends
     with" (module doc "Fixture provenance", the `CleanStop` arm comment).
     Update every line citation into `responses_tool_call.txt` (78, 81-93,
     96, 99) to the new line numbers.
   - b. `tests/responses_wire.rs`: the `sse()` helper stops appending
     `data: [DONE]`. Correct its doc comment.
4. **`tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt`.** Change the
   paragraph that says `responses_tool_call.txt`'s `[DONE]` is "unexplained"
   and "a follow-up" so that it points to SMA-585's resolution. Rename its
   "Two deliberate edits" list to the same Removed / Added structure.
5. **`CONTRIBUTING.md`.** Add a short "Wire-format fixtures" section:
   - A fixture header states its provenance: CAPTURED (endpoint, model,
     date) or HAND-AUTHORED.
   - A CAPTURED header lists every edit from the raw capture in two parts,
     Removed and Added. When a part is empty, the header says "nothing".
   - Do not add a line that the wire did not send to make a fixture match a
     sibling.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-providers-openai --all-features` and
  `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance` pass with no
  changed assertion.
- `grep -rn 'DONE' ` over the Responses fixtures, `responses_wire.rs` and
  the `openai_responses` module returns only header or doc text, not a
  `data: [DONE]` line or a `done()` call.
- Each line citation in `conformance.rs` points to the event it names.
- The CI gates in `CLAUDE.md` pass (`fmt`, `clippy`, `docs`,
  `markdown-lint`).

## Book and README

No book or README edit. The change is internal to tests, fixtures and
contributor policy, and it changes no public API.

## Left to the builder

- The exact wording of the headers and of the `CONTRIBUTING.md` section.
- Where in `CONTRIBUTING.md` the section goes.

# SMA-585: The Responses API sends no `data: [DONE]` (design)

## Intent

The OpenAI Responses fixtures must not claim more than the wire sent.
`responses_tool_call.txt` is labelled CAPTURED and lists every trim from the
raw capture, but it ends with `data: [DONE]` and its header does not explain
that line. The header structure has a place for removals and no place for
additions, so the line went unrecorded.

These fixtures are load-bearing. SMA-522 went wrong because a fixture was
derived and not captured. A CAPTURED label that overstates its file erodes
the reason the label exists.

## Evidence

- **2026-08-22** (from SMA-562): four `curl` captures against
  `/v1/responses` (`gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-5-mini`, a `background: true`
  request, a resumed stream). None contains `[DONE]`.
- **2026-11-21** (this ticket, 16:58 UTC, `openai-version: 2020-10-01`):
  four more captures. Each ends on its terminal event followed by `\n\n`.
  None contains the string `DONE` anywhere.

  | Request | Model | Terminal event |
  |---|---|---|
  | one `get_weather` tool (same shape as the 2026-08-20 fixture) | `gpt-4o-mini` | `response.completed` |
  | plain text | `gpt-4o-mini` | `response.completed` |
  | reasoning with `summary: auto` | `gpt-5-mini` | `response.completed` |
  | `max_output_tokens: 16` | `gpt-4o-mini` | `response.incomplete` |

- No raw copy of the 2026-08-20 capture exists in the repo or in any spec or
  plan. What the endpoint sent on that date cannot be proven. Two later
  captures on two dates speak against "OpenAI sent it then stopped".
- The other four `responses_*.txt` fixtures have no provenance header. The
  SMA-316 spec (`2026-05-26-sma-316-openai-provider-design.md`, line 365)
  says they are "Hand-authored". Their `[DONE]` is an assumption copied from
  the Chat Completions shape.
- The parser does not need the sentinel. SMA-562 served the byte-faithful
  capture through the wiremock harness with and without `[DONE]`, and the
  stream ended identically. async-openai ends the stream on body end.

The raw 2026-11-21 captures are not committed. They are evidence for this
decision, and the table above records what they show.

## Goals

1. No Responses fixture or Responses test body sends `data: [DONE]`.
2. Every Responses fixture header states its provenance: CAPTURED or
   HAND-AUTHORED.
3. The header convention records additions as well as removals, and the rule
   is written down once in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
4. Every cross-reference to a fixture (line numbers, doc comments) stays
   true after the edit.

## Non-goals

- Chat Completions fixtures and tests (`chat_*.txt`, `cancellation.rs`,
  `chat_wire.rs`). Chat Completions does send `[DONE]`.
- Replacing the fixtures with the new captures (approach B, rejected below).
- Fixture headers in other provider crates. The `CONTRIBUTING.md` rule
  applies to them from now on; this ticket does not audit them.
- Production code. `ResponsesTranslator` handles both shapes.

## Anti-goals

- A test that passes only because of `[DONE]`. If a test changes behaviour
  when the sentinel goes, stop and investigate. Do not add the line back.
- Changing any asserted id, model or token count.

## Approaches

- **A. Correct the existing files (chosen).** Keep the 2026-08-20
  transcription and the current hand-authored values. Remove the sentinel,
  restructure the headers, and update the cross-references. No test
  assertion changes.
- **B. Replace with the new captures (rejected).** This gives byte-faithful
  files for three shapes. But the tests and the conformance suite assert on
  the current ids, models and token counts, so many assertions must change.
  `response.failed` and a content-filter refusal cannot be triggered on
  demand, so two fixtures stay hand-authored anyway. The diff is too large
  for a Low-priority ticket.
- **C. Add notes and keep `[DONE]` (rejected).** A CAPTURED file would still
  carry a line that the wire does not send. That is the defect this ticket
  removes.

Sven picked A on 2026-11-21.

## Design

All paths are relative to `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/` unless
stated otherwise.

1. **`tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt`.** Remove the trailing
   `data: [DONE]` line. Replace "Three kinds of trimming from the raw
   capture" with an "Edits from the raw capture" section that has two fixed
   parts:
   - **Removed:** the three existing trims, with their text kept.
   - **Added:** "nothing".
   Add a dated correction note: until 2026-11-21 this file ended with
   `data: [DONE]`, which no header entry accounted for. The note gives the
   evidence above in short form and says the line was removed on 2026-11-21.
2. **The four hand-authored fixtures** (`responses_reasoning_then_text.txt`,
   `responses_incomplete_length.txt`, `responses_incomplete_filter.txt`,
   `responses_failed.txt`). Remove the trailing `data: [DONE]`. Add a short
   `:` comment header: HAND-AUTHORED under SMA-316, not captured; the event
   shapes follow the async-openai types; the stream ends on the terminal
   event with no `[DONE]`, as the 2026-08-22 and 2026-11-21 captures show.
3. **Responses test bodies.**
   - a. `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs`, module
     `openai_responses`: remove `done()` and its two uses (`CleanStop`,
     `ToolCallCleanStop`). Correct the doc comments that cite `[DONE]` as
     "the stream terminator every committed fixture in this crate ends
     with" (module doc "Fixture provenance", the `CleanStop` arm comment).
     Update every line citation into `responses_tool_call.txt` (78, 81-93,
     96, 99) to the new line numbers.
   - b. `tests/responses_wire.rs`: the `sse()` helper stops appending
     `data: [DONE]`. Correct its doc comment.
4. **`tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt`.** Change the
   paragraph that says `responses_tool_call.txt`'s `[DONE]` is "unexplained"
   and "a follow-up" so that it points to SMA-585's resolution. Rename its
   "Two deliberate edits" list to the same Removed / Added structure.
5. **`CONTRIBUTING.md`.** Add a short "Wire-format fixtures" section:
   - A fixture header states its provenance: CAPTURED (endpoint, model,
     date) or HAND-AUTHORED.
   - A CAPTURED header lists every edit from the raw capture in two parts,
     Removed and Added. When a part is empty, the header says "nothing".
   - Do not add a line that the wire did not send to make a fixture match a
     sibling.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-providers-openai --all-features` and
  `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance` pass with no
  changed assertion.
- `grep -rn 'DONE' ` over the Responses fixtures, `responses_wire.rs` and
  the `openai_responses` module returns only header or doc text, not a
  `data: [DONE]` line or a `done()` call.
- Each line citation in `conformance.rs` points to the event it names.
- The CI gates in `CLAUDE.md` pass (`fmt`, `clippy`, `docs`,
  `markdown-lint`).

## Book and README

No book or README edit. The change is internal to tests, fixtures and
contributor policy, and it changes no public API.

## Left to the builder

- The exact wording of the headers and of the `CONTRIBUTING.md` section.
- Where in `CONTRIBUTING.md` the section goes.

The new CONTRIBUTING rule also cannot express that kind of edit, and it does not address the root cause of the four hand-authored files.

  - **The "Added: nothing" edit list is probably incomplete: `responses_tool_call.txt` appears to have its keys reordered to match its siblings** - The header calls the file "a literal transcription" (`responses_tool_call.txt:29`). Design step 1 keeps the three trims as the full Removed list and adds "Added: nothing". But the key order in the file is not the order of the byte-faithful capture of the same endpoint and model, taken two days later:

    | Why it matters: The ticket exists to make a CAPTURED label truthful. The new CONTRIBUTING rule says a CAPTURED header "lists every edit". The flagship fixture would break that rule on the day it lands. | Suggested fix: Before you write the header, diff the fixture's key order against the 2026-11-21 `get_weather` capture (same request shape, same model). If they differ, record the reorder as an edit, remove the word "literal", and give the edit structure a third part (see the MAJOR finding on the CONTRIBUTING rule). Also correct the root-cause sentence in Intent ("no place for additions"). The cause is wider: the transcription was conformed to the sibling files.
  
  ### MAJOR
  - **The spec repeats the evidence gap that caused this ticket** - Evidence says "No raw copy of the 2026-08-20 capture exists ... cannot be proven". Then lines 42-43 decide not to commit the 2026-11-21 captures, and give only a summary table. The SMA-562 spec (§9, lines 490-497) did the same, which is why nobody can check 2026-08-20 today. The SMA-522 spec has precedent for doing better: "Appendix A — captured traces" (line 439). | Why it matters: The next auditor cannot verify "None contains the string DONE", and cannot settle the BLOCKER. | Suggested fix: Add an appendix to this spec. For each of the four captures, include the redacted response headers, the last event verbatim, the trailing bytes (for example `...}\n\n<EOF>`), and the curl exit status.     - (e) Inline wire bytes in test code are not covered. `responses_wire.rs` `sse()` and the conformance helpers carried the same `[DONE]` assumption.
    | Why it matters: The rule is the only thing that stops this from happening again, and it does not cover the failure that actually occurred. | Suggested fix:

Each CAPTURED event has a unique `sequence_number` (2, 3-7, 8, 9, 10). | Suggested fix: Cite by `sequence_number`, not by line. # SMA-585: The Responses API sends no `data: [DONE]` (design)

## Intent

The OpenAI Responses fixtures must not claim more than the wire sent.
`responses_tool_call.txt` is labelled CAPTURED and calls itself "a literal
transcription of a real capture". Its header lists every trim, but the file
has two edits that the header does not record:

1. It ends with `data: [DONE]`, which no capture of this endpoint contains.
2. Its JSON keys are in a different order from the wire. The order matches
   the hand-authored sibling fixtures (see Appendix A).

The root cause is wider than "the header has no place for additions". The
transcription was made to look like its siblings, and the header structure
could record only removals. These fixtures are load-bearing. SMA-522 went
wrong because a fixture was derived and not captured. A CAPTURED label that
overstates its file erodes the reason the label exists.

## Evidence

- **2026-08-22** (from SMA-562): four `curl` captures against
  `/v1/responses` (`gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-5-mini`, a `background: true`
  request, a resumed stream). None contains `[DONE]`.
  `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt` is one of them, byte-faithful.
- **2026-11-21** (this ticket): four more captures. The script ran with
  `set -euo pipefail`, so a curl error or a `--max-time` stop would have
  ended it. All four completed, so each curl exited 0 when the server closed
  the stream. Each file ends on its terminal event followed by `\n\n`, and
  none contains the string `DONE`. Appendix A records the details.
- No raw copy of the 2026-08-20 capture exists in the repo or in any spec or
  plan. What the endpoint sent on that date cannot be proven. Two later
  captures on two dates speak against "OpenAI sent it then stopped".
- The other four `responses_*.txt` fixtures have no provenance header. The
  SMA-316 spec (`2026-05-26-sma-316-openai-provider-design.md`, line 365)
  says they are "Hand-authored". Their `[DONE]` is framing copied from the
  Chat Completions shape.
- `[DONE]` and end of body are equivalent for every Responses terminal event.
  This follows from the code, not only from the SMA-562 probe:
  - async-openai 0.43.0 `src/client.rs:846-873`: on `[DONE]` the loop does
    `break`; on end of body the loop ends. Both drop the sender.
  - `src/backend/responses.rs:71`: the driver returns on `None`.
  - `src/backend/responses.rs:695-702`: `response.failed` yields `Err`, and
    the driver returns before it reads more.
- The repo has no first-party capture of Chat Completions. The
  `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt` capture is from a LiteLLM proxy. This spec
  does not depend on what Chat Completions sends.

## Goals

1. No fixture or test body presents `[DONE]` as OpenAI Responses wire
   behaviour.
2. Every Responses fixture header states its provenance and records every
   edit from its source.
3. A contributor rule in `CONTRIBUTING.md` records additions and changes as
   well as removals, and covers hand-authored files and inline wire helpers.
4. Every cross-reference to these fixtures in code and fixture headers stays
   true after the edit. Dated design documents under `docs/superpowers/**`
   are records of their time and are not edited.
5. Tolerance of a trailing `[DONE]` stays covered by one labelled test,
   because `base_url` is advertised for OpenAI-compatible servers
   (`src/builder.rs:72`).

## Non-goals

- Chat Completions fixtures and tests (`chat_*.txt`, `cancellation.rs`,
  `chat_wire.rs`).
- Replacing the fixtures with the new captures (approach B, rejected below).
- Restoring the wire key order in `responses_tool_call.txt`. The 2026-08-20
  order is unknown; a reorder to the 2026-11-21 order would be a second
  reconstruction from a different capture. The header records the change
  instead.
- Auditing fixtures in other crates. Files that do not follow the new rule
  on merge day go to a Linear follow-up (see Open items).
- Production code. `ResponsesTranslator` handles both shapes.

## Anti-goals

- A test that passes only because of `[DONE]`. If a test changes behaviour
  when the sentinel goes, stop and investigate. Do not add the line back.
- Changing any asserted id, model or token count.

## Approaches

- **A. Correct the existing files (chosen).** Keep the 2026-08-20
  transcription and the current hand-authored values. Remove the sentinel,
  record every edit in the headers, and update the cross-references. No test
  assertion changes.
- **B. Replace with the new captures (rejected).** The tests and the
  conformance suite assert on the current ids, models and token counts, so
  many assertions must change. `response.failed` and a content-filter
  refusal cannot be triggered on demand, so two fixtures stay hand-authored
  anyway. The diff is too large for a Low-priority ticket.
- **C. Add notes and keep `[DONE]` (rejected).** A CAPTURED file would still
  carry a line that the wire does not send.

Sven picked A on 2026-11-21.

## Design

Paths are relative to `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/` unless
stated otherwise.

### 1. `tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt`

- Remove the trailing `data: [DONE]` line.
- Remove the word "literal" from the `event:` paragraph, and change "unlike
  this directory's other `responses_*.txt` fixtures" so that it also names
  `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt`, which keeps `event:` lines too.
- Replace "Three kinds of trimming from the raw capture" with "Edits from
  the raw capture", in three fixed parts:
  - **Removed:** the three existing trims, with their text kept.
  - **Added:** nothing.
  - **Changed:** the JSON key order. The file puts `type` and
    `sequence_number` first and `item.type` before `item.id`, to match the
    hand-authored siblings. The 2026-08-22 and 2026-11-21 captures put
    `type` first and the other event keys in alphabetical order, and
    `item.id` before `item.type`. The 2026-08-20 order is not on record.
    The parser does not depend on key order.
- Add a dated correction note: until 2026-11-21 this file ended with a
  `[DONE]` sentinel line and had a changed key order, and the header
  recorded neither. The note gives the evidence in short form and points to

   the hand-authored sibling fixtures (see Appendix A).

  ended it. All four completed, so each curl exited 0 when the server closed
  the stream. Each file ends on its terminal event followed by `\n\n`, and

  `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt` capture is from a LiteLLM proxy. This spec
  does not depend on what Chat Completions sends.

## Goals

1. No fixture or test body presents `[DONE]` as OpenAI Responses wire
   behaviour.
2. Every Responses fixture header states its provenance and records every
   edit from its source.
3. A contributor rule in `CONTRIBUTING.md` records additions and changes as
   well as removals, and covers hand-authored files and inline wire helpers.
4. Every cross-reference to these fixtures in code and fixture headers stays
   true after the edit. Dated design documents under `docs/superpowers/**`
   are records of their time and are not edited.
5. Tolerance of a trailing `[DONE]` stays covered by one labelled test,
   because `base_url` is advertised for OpenAI-compatible servers
   (`src/builder.rs:72`).

## Non-goals

- Chat Completions fixtures and tests (`chat_*.txt`, `cancellation.rs`,
  `chat_wire.rs`).
- Replacing the fixtures with the new captures (approach B, rejected below).
- Restoring the wire key order in `responses_tool_call.txt`. The 2026-08-20
  order is unknown; a reorder to the 2026-11-21 order would be a second
  reconstruction from a different capture. The header records the change
  instead.
- Auditing fixtures in other crates. Files that do not follow the new rule
  on merge day go to a Linear follow-up (see Open items).
- Production code. `ResponsesTranslator` handles both shapes.

## Anti-goals

- A test that passes only because of `[DONE]`. If a test changes behaviour
  when the sentinel goes, stop and investigate. Do not add the line back.
- Changing any asserted id, model or token count.

## Approaches

- **A. Correct the existing files (chosen).** Keep the 2026-08-20
  transcription and the current hand-authored values. Remove the sentinel,
  record every edit in the headers, and update the cross-references. No test
  assertion changes.
- **B. Replace with the new captures (rejected).** The tests and the
  conformance suite assert on the current ids, models and token counts, so
  many assertions must change. `response.failed` and a content-filter
  refusal cannot be triggered on demand, so two fixtures stay hand-authored
  anyway. The diff is too large for a Low-priority ticket.
- **C. Add notes and keep `[DONE]` (rejected).** A CAPTURED file would still
  carry a line that the wire does not send.

Add a "Wire-format fixtures" section to `CONTRIBUTING.md`:

  date), HAND-AUTHORED, or CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts.

  three parts: Removed, Added, Changed (reorder, reformat, value edits).
  When a part is empty, it says "nothing".

  each shape: a capture or a vendored type. Do not copy framing from a
  different endpoint or API.

  fixture match a sibling. If you must, record it under Changed.

  comment header. A format with no comment syntax records its provenance in
  the doc comment of the test that loads it. Inline wire helpers in test

# SMA-585: The Responses API sends no `data: [DONE]` (design)

## Intent

The OpenAI Responses fixtures must not claim more than the wire sent.
`responses_tool_call.txt` is labelled CAPTURED and lists every trim from the
raw capture, but it ends with `data: [DONE]` and its header does not explain
that line. The header structure has a place for removals and no place for
additions, so the line went unrecorded.

These fixtures are load-bearing. SMA-522 went wrong because a fixture was
derived and not captured. A CAPTURED label that overstates its file erodes
the reason the label exists.

## Evidence

- **2026-08-22** (from SMA-562): four `curl` captures against
  `/v1/responses` (`gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-5-mini`, a `background: true`
  request, a resumed stream). None contains `[DONE]`.
- **2026-11-21** (this ticket, 16:58 UTC, `openai-version: 2020-10-01`):
  four more captures. Each ends on its terminal event followed by `\n\n`.
  None contains the string `DONE` anywhere.

  | Request | Model | Terminal event |
  |---|---|---|
  | one `get_weather` tool (same shape as the 2026-08-20 fixture) | `gpt-4o-mini` | `response.completed` |
  | plain text | `gpt-4o-mini` | `response.completed` |
  | reasoning with `summary: auto` | `gpt-5-mini` | `response.completed` |
  | `max_output_tokens: 16` | `gpt-4o-mini` | `response.incomplete` |

- No raw copy of the 2026-08-20 capture exists in the repo or in any spec or
  plan. What the endpoint sent on that date cannot be proven. Two later
  captures on two dates speak against "OpenAI sent it then stopped".
- The other four `responses_*.txt` fixtures have no provenance header. The
  SMA-316 spec (`2026-05-26-sma-316-openai-provider-design.md`, line 365)
  says they are "Hand-authored". Their `[DONE]` is an assumption copied from
  the Chat Completions shape.
- The parser does not need the sentinel. SMA-562 served the byte-faithful
  capture through the wiremock harness with and without `[DONE]`, and the
  stream ended identically. async-openai ends the stream on body end.

The raw 2026-11-21 captures are not committed. They are evidence for this
decision, and the table above records what they show.

## Goals

1. No Responses fixture or Responses test body sends `data: [DONE]`.
2. Every Responses fixture header states its provenance: CAPTURED or
   HAND-AUTHORED.
3. The header convention records additions as well as removals, and the rule
   is written down once in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
4. Every cross-reference to a fixture (line numbers, doc comments) stays
   true after the edit.

## Non-goals

- Chat Completions fixtures and tests (`chat_*.txt`, `cancellation.rs`,
  `chat_wire.rs`). Chat Completions does send `[DONE]`.
- Replacing the fixtures with the new captures (approach B, rejected below).
- Fixture headers in other provider crates. The `CONTRIBUTING.md` rule
  applies to them from now on; this ticket does not audit them.
- Production code. `ResponsesTranslator` handles both shapes.

## Anti-goals

- A test that passes only because of `[DONE]`. If a test changes behaviour
  when the sentinel goes, stop and investigate. Do not add the line back.
- Changing any asserted id, model or token count.

## Approaches

- **A. Correct the existing files (chosen).** Keep the 2026-08-20
  transcription and the current hand-authored values. Remove the sentinel,
  restructure the headers, and update the cross-references. No test
  assertion changes.
- **B. Replace with the new captures (rejected).** This gives byte-faithful
  files for three shapes. But the tests and the conformance suite assert on
  the current ids, models and token counts, so many assertions must change.
  `response.failed` and a content-filter refusal cannot be triggered on
  demand, so two fixtures stay hand-authored anyway. The diff is too large
  for a Low-priority ticket.
- **C. Add notes and keep `[DONE]` (rejected).** A CAPTURED file would still
  carry a line that the wire does not send. That is the defect this ticket
  removes.

Sven picked A on 2026-11-21.

## Design

All paths are relative to `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/` unless
stated otherwise.

1. **`tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt`.** Remove the trailing
   `data: [DONE]` line. Replace "Three kinds of trimming from the raw
   capture" with an "Edits from the raw capture" section that has two fixed
   parts:
   - **Removed:** the three existing trims, with their text kept.
   - **Added:** "nothing".
   Add a dated correction note: until 2026-11-21 this file ended with
   `data: [DONE]`, which no header entry accounted for. The note gives the
   evidence above in short form and says the line was removed on 2026-11-21.
2. **The four hand-authored fixtures** (`responses_reasoning_then_text.txt`,
   `responses_incomplete_length.txt`, `responses_incomplete_filter.txt`,
   `responses_failed.txt`). Remove the trailing `data: [DONE]`. Add a short
   `:` comment header: HAND-AUTHORED under SMA-316, not captured; the event
   shapes follow the async-openai types; the stream ends on the terminal
   event with no `[DONE]`, as the 2026-08-22 and 2026-11-21 captures show.
3. **Responses test bodies.**
   - a. `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs`, module
     `openai_responses`: remove `done()` and its two uses (`CleanStop`,
     `ToolCallCleanStop`). Correct the doc comments that cite `[DONE]` as
     "the stream terminator every committed fixture in this crate ends
     with" (module doc "Fixture provenance", the `CleanStop` arm comment).
     Update every line citation into `responses_tool_call.txt` (78, 81-93,
     96, 99) to the new line numbers.
   - b. `tests/responses_wire.rs`: the `sse()` helper stops appending
     `data: [DONE]`. Correct its doc comment.
4. **`tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt`.** Change the
   paragraph that says `responses_tool_call.txt`'s `[DONE]` is "unexplained"
   and "a follow-up" so that it points to SMA-585's resolution. Rename its
   "Two deliberate edits" list to the same Removed / Added structure.
5. **`CONTRIBUTING.md`.** Add a short "Wire-format fixtures" section:
   - A fixture header states its provenance: CAPTURED (endpoint, model,
     date) or HAND-AUTHORED.
   - A CAPTURED header lists every edit from the raw capture in two parts,
     Removed and Added. When a part is empty, the header says "nothing".
   - Do not add a line that the wire did not send to make a fixture match a
     sibling.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-providers-openai --all-features` and
  `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance` pass with no
  changed assertion.
- `grep -rn 'DONE' ` over the Responses fixtures, `responses_wire.rs` and
  the `openai_responses` module returns only header or doc text, not a
  `data: [DONE]` line or a `done()` call.
- Each line citation in `conformance.rs` points to the event it names.
- The CI gates in `CLAUDE.md` pass (`fmt`, `clippy`, `docs`,
  `markdown-lint`).

## Book and README

No book or README edit. The change is internal to tests, fixtures and
contributor policy, and it changes no public API.

## Left to the builder

- The exact wording of the headers and of the `CONTRIBUTING.md` section.
- Where in `CONTRIBUTING.md` the section goes.

## Gate 1: approve the spec

I made a new capture with the script you ran. The capture settles the main question: none of the four streams from 2026-11-21 contains `[DONE]`. Each one ends on its terminal event and then the end of the body. The spec is at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-sma-585-responses-done-sentinel-design.md` and has an appendix that records the captures.

**Challenger verdict: approve with changes.** It found no test that needs `[DONE]`. In async-openai 0.43.0, `[DONE]` and end of body end the stream the same way for every terminal event.

**Findings I applied**

- **BLOCKER, confirmed by the capture.** The file `responses_tool_call.txt` has a second edit that its header does not record: the JSON key order. The wire puts `type` first and then the other keys in alphabetical order. The fixture puts `sequence_number` second, the same as its hand-authored siblings. The header will record this under a new "Changed" part, and the word "literal" goes. I do not restore the wire order, because nobody recorded the order from 2026-08-20.
- The convention now has three parts: Removed / Added / Changed. The `CONTRIBUTING.md` rule also covers hand-authored files ("name the source of each shape; do not copy framing from another endpoint") and inline test helpers. `CLAUDE.md` gets a one-line pointer to it.
- The headers for `responses_failed.txt` and `responses_incomplete_filter.txt` do not claim that a capture supports them, because no capture of those events exists.
- A new labelled test, `trailing_done_sentinel_is_tolerated`, keeps the support for OpenAI-compatible servers that send `[DONE]`. A guard test makes sure that no `[DONE]` line comes back into a fixture.
- `done()` has three uses, not two. The line citations in `conformance.rs` change to `sequence_number` citations, so they do not move when a header changes. I added the other stale cross-references to the edit list.
- I added a rollout note: release-plz will give `providers-openai` a patch bump and the facade a cascade bump. That is harmless.

**Findings I rejected:** none. Two parts were narrowed. The dated `docs/superpowers/**` documents are records of their time, so I do not edit them. I also do not audit the fixtures in other crates in this ticket.

2. The spec has an open item: a Linear follow-up for fixtures in other crates that break the new rule on merge day. Examples are the LiteLLM CAPTURED fixtures and `chat_text_usage_trailing.txt`. Do you want me to file it?

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Step Granularity

**Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus
```

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.
